questions.q: What single question does a system context diagram answer, per this lesson?
options: What internal Flows and triggers automate this org?
What is this system, and what external actors and systems does it exchange information with?
What is the exact field-level security configuration of each object?
In what order do API calls happen during one transaction?
questions.explain: A system context diagram draws the system as one box and shows every external actor and system crossing its boundary — it establishes what the system is and what it touches, nothing about internals.

questions.q: Why does a system context diagram deliberately show nothing about what's inside the central box?
options: Because Salesforce prohibits documenting internal configuration
Because establishing the system's boundary and external connections is the diagram's whole job; internal detail belongs to other, lower-zoom diagrams
Because internal detail is classified information
Because the box represents a database table, not a system
questions.explain: The context diagram's purpose is to establish the boundary before anyone discusses internals — showing internal detail here would blur the one job this diagram is meant to do.

questions.q: In the C4 model referenced in this lesson, which zoom level does a system context diagram correspond to?
options: Code
Component
Container
Context — the top, widest zoom level of the four
questions.explain: The C4 model's four levels run Context, Container, Component, Code from widest to narrowest zoom; a system context diagram corresponds to the top Context level.

questions.q: A company's Salesforce org exchanges nightly batch invoice data with NetSuite and receives real-time lead pushes from Marketo. On a system context diagram, how should this be represented?
options: NetSuite and Marketo should not appear on the diagram since they aren't Salesforce features
As a single combined box labeled 'External Systems' with no further detail
As separate boxes for NetSuite and Marketo, each connected to the central Salesforce box by a labeled line showing what crosses it
As internal objects inside the Salesforce box
questions.explain: Each external system gets its own box around the central system box, connected by a labeled line describing what crosses the boundary — that inventory of external connections is exactly what a context diagram is for.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a system context diagram typically comes first in a documentation set?
options: Because it is the only diagram regulators require

Because every more detailed diagram (ERD, data-flow, sequence) describes something happening inside one of the context diagram's boxes or along one of its connecting lines, so the context diagram gives the reader a map for where detail fits
Because it takes the least time to draw and should be done first for that reason alone
Because sequence diagrams must be drawn before context diagrams are legally valid
questions.explain: A reader who hasn't seen the context diagram has no map for where a detailed data-flow or sequence diagram even fits — the wide view orients the reader before the narrower diagrams add detail.
